structured_output.strongest_bear_case: City Protocol (formerly Cooking City) is a real project backed by Dragonfly, Jump Crypto and CMT Digital, with about $11M raised (announced Aug 26, 2026). That real news makes the name easy to trade on. I could not find anything linking this contract (3TrSG…) to the project: the official gitbook docs have no CT token, contract address or tokenomics, and the funding coverage I read doesn't name one either. Search results put CT's launch date at Sept 28, 2026, while this pool opened Sept 22. A $1.6M valuation with everything circulating (about 100B tokens) is hard to square with a project that raised $11M. A second 'City Protocol' CT (E84F…) was created about 3.7 hours earlier and now has $0.02 liquidity, which looks like serial copycat launches (one drained or abandoned). The CT ticker also collides with Concrete's real CT token announcement: a Solana 'Concrete' CT is trading at the same time with almost the same past-hour volume ($6.41M vs $6.42M), so buyers may be confusing the two. The trading pattern also looks unhealthy: $23M traded in under 5 hours against about $265k liquidity (the pool turns over about 24 times an hour, a wash-trading warning sign), and about 4,980 unique buyers against only 416 unique sellers, which looks like a few holders selling into broad demand. Holder data adds to the risk: GeckoTerminal shows the top 10 holding 89.9%, a 66-wallet network is linked by transfers, GMGN flags 14 bundlers, and RugCheck flags liquidity as unlocked on one market. If this isn't the official token, any official announcement of a different contract would likely crash it.

structured_output.coverage_notes: X returned HTTP 402, so I could not check whether the official account posted this contract. That is the key missing piece. The Sept 28 launch date comes from a search-result summary (ICO-calendar-type sources), not the project itself, and I did not verify it directly. The gitbook docs have no token information. I did not access Telegram or Discord. Points against the bear case: the contract can't mint new tokens or freeze wallets, there is no tax, no paid DexScreener promotion, GMGN shows a 0% bot share and no known promoter (KOL) wallets, and GMGN reports the LP burned (this conflicts with RugCheck). The launch was a direct Meteora launch that moved to the main exchange immediately (created and migrated at the same second), which a real team could do. The X rename (cookingcityHQ to cityprotocolHQ) is a real rebrand, not a recycled account.
